summary: Milestone 2026.10.722 completed 9 experiments (1 compute-bound, 8 synthesis-only) across 143.7 total wall-time minutes (averaging 16 minutes per experiment) reconstructed from disk-mtime fallback data. Execution wall time was led by synthesis-only tasks—reconciling fourteen outcomes and deciding research continuations (26.97 minutes), collecting fresh ARC supervisor observations (18.82 minutes), mapping direct transactions to KV260 (18.25 minutes), and freezing direct-service methods with fourteen task contracts (17.61 minutes)—alongside the sole compute-bound task inspecting CUDA evidence with the qualified typed reader (18.91 minutes). With gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks recorded as false, the point-in-time monitor reading of 0% GPU utilization (2MB allocated) on the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 reflects expected post-run idle state for non-GPU synthesis workloads, and single-model compute execution correctly avoided multi-model DualGPURunner dispatch.
bottlenecks_identified: Synthesis-only tasks accounted for 8 of 9 completed experiments and four of the top five slowest runs totaling 81.65 minutes out of 143.7 total wall-time minutes, led by fourteen-outcome reconciliation (26.97 minutes), ARC supervisor observation collection (18.82 minutes), and KV260 hardware transaction mapping (18.25 minutes).

The sole compute-bound task ('Inspect changed CUDA evidence with the already qualified typed reader') required 18.91 minutes, but available experiment receipts lack intra-task phase telemetry (environment setup, evidence parsing, model execution, artifact serialization) to localize runtime latency.

Long-running synthesis tasks (fourteen-outcome reconciliation, adapter-withheld ARC observation collection, hardware transaction mapping, and contract freezing) executed serially without incremental receipt caching or evidence memoization when upstream artifacts were unchanged.
Milestone timing analysis relied on disk-mtime fallback reconstruction because the live git-log path found 0 commits in the milestone interval.
improvements_suggested: Implement incremental receipt caching and evidence memoization for multi-minute synthesis tasks (outcome reconciliation, ARC supervisor observation collection, hardware transaction mapping, and task contract freezing) when upstream inputs remain unchanged.
Instrument multi-minute synthesis and compute-bound tasks with granular intra-phase execution timers (setup, execution, verification, serialization) to pinpoint operational latency.
Persist explicit synchronous execution timestamps (start, completion, duration) directly into experiment receipts to eliminate dependence on disk-mtime fallback reconstruction.
Sample continuous in-flight accelerator utilization and memory telemetry during compute-bound execution intervals rather than relying solely on post-run point-in-time GPU monitor polling.
Maintain strict DualGPURunner dispatch boundaries restricted to concurrent multi-model pipelines, avoiding unnecessary invocation overhead for single-model or synthesis workloads.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Deploy incremental receipt caching and evidence memoization for long-running synthesis workflows (fourteen-outcome reconciliation, ARC observation collection, and hardware transaction mapping) when upstream artifacts are unchanged.
Instrument long-running synthesis tasks and compute-bound workloads with granular intra-task phase timers.

meta_reflection: Across 9 completed experiments and 143.7 minutes of milestone wall time, execution was dominated by synthesis-only tasks averaging 16 minutes per experiment, with the sole compute-bound task finishing second overall at 18.91 minutes behind fourteen-outcome reconciliation (26.97 minutes). Point-in-time GPU monitoring showed 0% utilization on the RTX 3090 as expected for non-GPU synthesis workloads, with gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks recorded as false. Operational improvements should target incremental receipt caching for unchanged upstream dependencies and granular intra-phase telemetry for multi-minute tasks, with estimated time savings conservatively held at 0% until empirically validated.
